flow.zh:
湖光水色的遙想
 Plitvice Lakes National Park,  Croatia
克羅埃西亞的普萊特維斯湖泊國家公園，由黒河和白河匯合，引出16座連續跌落，藍綠晶透的湖泊。交織著90多個大小高低不等，形態各異的瀑布，或垂懸狂瀉、或盤纏如網。流水冲擊石灰岩層和晶瑩愓透的湖面，濺成水花翩翩、煙霧裊裊。湖岸的藓苔、藻類和青草，與環湖蓊鬰的冷杉、白松、三毛櫸，加上飄浮的白雲，襯托出瑰麗的湖光水色。漫步棧道，泛舟湖上，看飛瀑、聽水聲……。
flow.en: Croatia's Plitvice Lakes National Park is formed by the confluence of the Black River and the White River, giving rise to sixteen lakes cascading one into the next, their waters a crystalline blue-green. Woven among them are more than ninety waterfalls of varying size and height and differing form—some plunging in a wild, hanging torrent, others tangled and webbed like netting. As the flowing water strikes the limestone shelves and the glittering, translucent surface of the lakes, it scatters into dancing spray and curling mist. The moss, algae, and grasses along the shore, together with the lush firs, white pines, and beeches encircling the lakes, and the drifting white clouds above, set off the resplendent color of the lake and its light. Walking the boardwalk, drifting by boat upon the lake, watching the flying falls, listening to the sound of the water……

points.zh: 嘉南平原是台灣最大的平原，北起虎尾溪，南至鹽水溪，長130公里，寬35公里，包括雲林，嘉義，台南三縣。整個平原地勢平坦，適宜農業發展，可惜平原上的河川大多不具灌漑之利。雖有北港溪，八掌溪，急水溪，曾文溪等河川穿越，但河流湍急，含沙量大，大雨一至，沙石順坡而下，淤積河道，洪水成災。早期農民深受水災，乾旱，鹽害之苦，只能勉强收成甘蔗，雜糧糊口。爲解决嘉南平原灌漑水源的問題，當時的日本政府興建嘉南大圳和烏山頭水庫 。烏山頭水庫是台灣最大人造湖 (又名珊瑚潭，因湖岸蜿蜒曲折，島嶼羅列，狀如美麗的綠色珊瑚礁)，由總督府工程師八田與一 (1882～1942) 設計監督，一九二〇年開工，克服惡劣困頓，瘴痢肆虐環境，一九三〇年完工。烏山頭水庫自曾文溪支流官田溪上游聚水，是嘉南大圳的主要水源。水源自烏山頭水庫流出後，分爲南北二幹線，北幹線跨急水溪，八掌溪，朴子溪到北港溪南岸，南幹線跨越官田溪，曾文溪至善化鎮接支線。嘉南大圳也自濁水溪進水，經舊虎尾溪南行與北幹線連接。如此在整個嘉南平原，建造出蜘蛛網般密佈的水路，這就是嘉南大圳。前總統李登輝常怨嘆：「很多人都不知道嘉南大圳究竟有多長。」給水路總長一萬公里，排水路總長六千公里，二者合計16000公里，等於繞地球半圈。嘉南大圳竣工後，嘉南平原水田大幅增加30倍，滋潤嘉南平原成爲台灣最大糧倉。而八田與一的專業堅持，全心服務精神，像嘉南大圳的滔滔流水，源源流進無數農民感恩的心坎，緬懷至今。因築壩技術特殊，儲水量爲當時東亞之冠，令全球土木界嘖嘖稱奇，美國工程學會特别將烏山頭水庫名爲「八田水庫」。
points.en: The Chianan Plain is Taiwan's largest plain, extending from the Huwei River in the north to the Yanshui River in the south, about 130 kilometers long and 35 kilometers wide, covering Yunlin, Chiayi, and Tainan counties. The whole plain is flat and well-suited for agriculture, but unfortunately most of the rivers crossing the plain were of little use for irrigation. Although rivers such as the Beigang, Bazhang, Jishui, and Zengwen pass through it, they flow swiftly and carry heavy sediment loads; when heavy rains came, sand and gravel would wash down the slopes, silting up the riverbeds and causing floods. In earlier times, farmers suffered greatly from floods, drought, and salt damage, barely managing to harvest sugarcane and coarse grains to survive. To solve the problem of irrigation water for the Chianan Plain, the Japanese colonial government at the time built the Chianan Irrigation Canal and the Wushantou Reservoir. Wushantou Reservoir is Taiwan's largest man-made lake (also called Coral Lake, because its winding shoreline and scattered islands resemble a beautiful green coral reef). It was designed and supervised by Governor-General's Office engineer Hatta Yoichi (1882-1942), begun in 1920, and completed in 1930 after overcoming harsh conditions and rampant disease. Wushantou Reservoir collects water from the upper reaches of the Guantian River, a tributary of the Zengwen River, and is the main water source for the Chianan Irrigation Canal. After leaving Wushantou Reservoir, the water divides into north and south main channels: the north channel crosses the Jishui, Bazhang, and Puzi rivers to reach the south bank of the Beigang River, while the south channel crosses the Guantian River and the Zengwen River to reach Shanhua and connect with branch channels. The Chianan Canal also draws water from the Zhuoshui River, flowing south via the old Huwei River to connect with the north channel. In this way, a spiderweb-like network of waterways was built across the entire Chianan Plain — this is the Chianan Irrigation Canal. Former President Lee Teng-hui often lamented: "Many people don't know just how long the Chianan Canal really is." The main supply channels total 10,000 kilometers in length, and the drainage channels total 6,000 kilometers, for a combined total of 16,000 kilometers — equivalent to half the circumference of the earth. After the completion of the Chianan Canal, irrigated paddy fields on the Chianan Plain increased thirtyfold, nourishing the plain into Taiwan's largest granary. Hatta Yoichi's professional dedication and wholehearted spirit of service, like the ceaseless flow of the Chianan Canal's waters, has flowed into the grateful hearts of countless farmers and is remembered to this day. Because of the reservoir's special dam-building technology, its water storage capacity was the largest in East Asia at the time, drawing admiration from civil engineers worldwide; the American Society of Civil Engineers specially named Wushantou Reservoir the "Hatta Dam."
